The draft describes a two-layer federated reference architecture (Local Discovery Plane and Federation Plane) with Federation Gateways, an Export Policy Engine and Federation Metadata Records for initial agent discovery; it is informational and defines no normative protocol formats.

Internet-Draft specifying a JSON Agent Identity Document at /.well-known/agent-identity.json on a provider-assigned hostname, with lifecycle status, dated expiring checks on the operator, and a request to register the well-known URI suffix; states it describes a practice in production at one provider.

The Internet-Draft defines three DNS TXT records (_mcp, _org-alter, _alter) for MCP server discovery, organisational identity, and a signed Ed25519 handle envelope, with Informational intended status and expiry on 12 April 2027.

Internet-Draft -08 published 14 October 2026, Intended Status Informational, defining a verifier-facing claim matrix format, row-outcome semantics (satisfied, unsatisfied, indeterminate, unsupported, not-evaluated, not-applicable) and dependency-closure rules for composed mappings. States it does not define a new agent protocol, token format, audit log or authorization system.
The draft specifies AIP, a delegation chain model with an attenuation invariant, a verification algorithm, JWT-chain and Biscuit encodings, and bindings for MCP, A2A and HTTP.

Internet-Draft draft-sweeney-wimse-credential-delegation-01, published 13 October 2026, Intended Status Standards Track, workgroup WIMSE; profiles RFC 8693, RFC 9449, RFC 9396 and OpenID CIBA for credential delegation to AI agents.

The Internet-Draft defines the Agent Delegation Receipt as a signed record of what a human principal authorized an AI agent to do, using a JWS profile over JCS-canonicalized JSON and a COSE_Sign1 profile, plus scope attenuation for delegation chains and a revocation registry with cascade semantics.

Individual-submission companion to the AAuth Protocol by Dick Hardt (Hellō); -00, marked Exploratory Draft, no known implementations. It replaces scope strings with resource-named operations in vocabularies (MCP, OpenAPI, gRPC, GraphQL, AsyncAPI, WSDL, OData), content-addressed R3 documents identified by SHA-256, and per-call proposals.

Internet-Draft defines ACIP, a YAML-based format and host-resolution behavior for coding-agent context sources, with source precedence, file matching, constraint/directive/preference distinctions, and a resolution receipt.

Internet-Draft -01 defines the 'knowledge-linkset' well-known URI serving an RFC 9264 link set of knowledge artefacts with optional SHA-256 digests and a profile URI; intended status Informational, expires 17 April 2027.

Internet-Draft defines the AgentInteractionRecord (AIR) as a COSE_Sign1 signed statement payload for material AI agent actions. It maps the Agent Operator to SCITT Issuer and an independent Evidence Custodian to Transparency Service, and defines registration policy, redaction receipts and regulatory mappings (EU AI Act Arts. 12/19, DORA, NIST AI RMF, MAS, PCI DSS, MiFID II).

Internet-Draft specifies a JSON agent-channel frame with a closed catalogue of kinds, identity attribution pair, provenance block, recipient scope expansion, and per-handle Server-Sent Events delivery with subscribe-time filters.

The Internet-Draft defines AAGV, a JSON interchange profile and deterministic validation algorithm for authority roots, consequential sinks, normal paths, revocation cut sets and snapshot edge state, with outcomes INVALID, INDETERMINATE, VALID_OPEN and VALID_CLOSED.

Internet-Draft draft-king-yew-choo-agentic-payments-01 published 8 October 2026, Intended Status Informational. It defines no protocol, wire format, or conformance requirements, and presents a server-side payment/entitlement gate (g*) and task state machine for agent-initiated paid asynchronous HTTP tasks.

Rosomakho (Zscaler); specifies workload metadata attributes delivered in JWT-based credentials or via an authenticated metadata endpoint, separate from the workload identifier.

The Internet-Draft defines HAACE, a protocol-neutral profile binding an exact agent action to identity status, authorization state, policy, assurance stage, evidence state, authority epoch, revocation state and oversight requirements, with fail-closed handling and non-bearer decision and execution receipts.

The draft defines a per-call proof for local tool invocation: a Call Authority outside the agent process issues short-lived, single-use proofs bound to the tool name and arguments through a canonical action digest (JCS + SHA-256), and the tool server rejects invocations lacking a valid proof. It includes an MCP stdio binding.
The AAE is a W3C Verifiable Credential signed as a compact JWS (EdDSA/Ed25519) with mandatory mandate, constraints and validity blocks; the key is named by a DID URL.

The Internet-Draft defines A2WP, where an AI Agent passes a credential offer or presentation request unchanged to a Wallet. The Wallet runs OpenID4VCI or OpenID4VP, and credentials, presentations and keys never reach the agent. The draft has Submit, Get and Cancel calls and an operation lifecycle of pending, completed, failed and cancelled.

Internet-Draft defines the Agent Decision Commitment: a salted hash commitment to a decision record, carried as a selectively disclosable claim in a payment mandate and registered with a transparency service, with bindings to three agent payment protocols and account-to-account credit transfers, plus a witnessed reciprocal exchange.
